doc.title: Bill Easley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 1, 2021

title: Music as livelihood and studying human behavior
summary: Easley says music pays his bills while his real interest is human behavior; recalls Cannonball's remark about people pretending to be hip.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: All right. When you describe what you do, because you’ve had a very versatile career, when you describe what you do, do you have a sort of short way of summing it up?

Well music is my livelihood. My life is about the study of human behavior, human growth and development, and I am 75 and I would like to become a psychiatrist but they told me I would have to go to school, but I have always been an amateur psychologist my whole life, and music is just what I do to pay my bills.

Being a musician and being in all these different situations, did your intense behavior at looking at other people’s behavior, did music give you a chance to observe a lot of different kinds of personalities?

Sure. And some people, you know they have certain things that they think are unique to musicians. By my study musicians are just people just like everybody else. And some of them, Cannonball made a statement one time on “Live to New York” and he talked about people who act like they’re supposed to be hip or something. Do you remember that statement?

I heard that as a teenager and it resonated in my head because he wasn’t talking about musicians per se but people in general, they just try to pretend that they’re something, you know, rather than being themselves.
